post.caption:
Chips are printed, not carved. A pattern is projected through a mask onto a light-sensitive wafer, then etched, recoated and printed again, dozens of layers deep. Printing smaller needs shorter wavelengths, and extreme ultraviolet machines make their light by hitting falling tin droplets with a laser twice each. One machine costs hundreds of millions and one company makes them. Cleanrooms are purer than an operating theatre because a single speck ruins the chip beneath it.
